clue.text: Dupe, ruined after deception, behaved badly

indicators.note: the reworked word is placed after the deception piece

parts.note: an act is a pretence, a piece of deception put on for show

indicators.note: a ruined word is wrecked, so its letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who was swindled and ruined by a con then went off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dupe' reads as the victim of the deception, but its letters, 'ruined' into EDUP, are the fodder; 'after' places them last.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an idiom for misbehaving, playing up like a naughty child.

clue.text: Turn up to perform

definitions.meaning: to arrive or come into view
to take a part on stage, as an actor does in a play

explanation.surface: An invitation to show up and do a turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the verb: to arrive or come into view, and to take part in a show as an actor.

clue.text: A car carries their odds and ends

indicators.note: in this down clue the car carries the other piece on top of it, so that piece comes first
the odd-numbered letters (first, third, fifth) of the word their are taken

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A motorist hauls around bits and pieces belonging to other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' takes T, E, R from THEIR; 'carries' sets them above MINI. 'odds and ends' looks like one phrase but splits: 'odds' is the indicator and 'ends' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end points of transport routes, the stations where lines finish.

clue.text: Ged rid of crazy underbids

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the next word are sent wild and reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to dump a bridge partner's foolish low bids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges UNDERBIDS. The page prints 'Ged', a slip for 'Get': 'Get rid of' is the definition. Underbidding is offering too little at bridge or auction.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to relieve of a load, freeing oneself of something unwanted.

clue.text: Get a lift from prayer

definitions.meaning: an elevator of open compartments on a loop that never stops
the Lord's Prayer, named from its Latin first words

explanation.surface: Someone finds an emotional uplift in praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' and 'from' are link words. A paternoster lift is a chain of open cars moving continuously up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A paternoster is both a continuously moving elevator and the Lord's Prayer, from its Latin opening words 'Our Father'.

clue.text: A voice in Schumann's first work conducted with love

indicators.note: the first letter of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a musical work
ran means conducted or managed, as one runs a business
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer performs a Schumann piece with great affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted' looks musical beside Schumann but means RAN, as in managed.
explanation.definitionFit: The soprano is the highest singing voice, one of the standard vocal ranges.

clue.text: Sound wine in a bag

indicators.note: the clue signals that the word for the wine is said out loud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: sack is an old name for dry white wine from Spain, drunk by Falstaff

explanation.surface: Decent wine served in a box or pouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like praise of the wine (sound wine = good wine) but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a pouch-like cavity in a plant or animal, a natural pouch.

clue.text: The best bishop? True!

parts.note: a plum job is the best, most sought-after one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cleric is the finest, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True!' sounds like agreement but is the definition: plumb in the builder's sense of perfectly vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that is plumb stands exactly upright, as true as a plumb line shows.

clue.text: Regalia thrown out in the republic

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A new regime discards the royal trappings after becoming a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges REGALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African country with a republican government.

clue.text: Outside broadcast children presented about ship that's haunted

indicators.note: the children piece goes around the ship piece

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in the biblical sense
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A TV crew and kids present a programme on a ghost ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container signal but belongs to the abbreviation 'Outside broadcast'; the real container indicator is 'about', giving SESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be haunted by a thought is to be preoccupied, unable to escape it.

clue.text: A flea is caught — it's brought back by a soldier

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed beside, after, the soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: brought back means the pieces are turned to read in the other direction

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
it's expands to it is

explanation.surface: A soldier catches a flea and brings it back from the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives SITIC. The definition completes a sentence: a flea is parasitic. 'by' places the turned letters beside the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas live on and feed off the blood of a host animal, the defining habit of a parasite.

clue.text: Encourages heads to use recognised governmental education services

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from each of the five words

explanation.surface: A call for school heads to use official education services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' looks like headteachers but takes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge is to press or spur someone on, a synonym for encourage.

clue.text: Cheers for a lady by European leaders

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
the leading two letters of the word European

explanation.surface: Toasting a woman alongside the heads of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is British informal for goodbye, not a toast. 'leaders' takes two letters here, E and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is casual British slang for a farewell, as is the French word of parting.

clue.text: Things seldom seen in first-rate pies, perhaps

parts.note: rare in the older sense of excellent, as in a rare old time
pie is an old name for the magpie, an example of a bird

explanation.surface: Something hard to find inside top-quality baked pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pies' suggests pastry, but a pie is a magpie, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare bird is an idiom for an unusual person or thing, something one hardly ever meets.

clue.text: Honest and decent plebs create confusion

indicators.note: the two words are thrown into confusion, their letters mixed together

explanation.surface: Ordinary people who are honest are said to sow disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'create' looks like the verb of the sentence but is anagram fodder with PLEBS; 'confusion' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A respectable person is upright and proper, of good character.

clue.text: Hopeless quest for good English chisel was misguided

indicators.note: misguided suggests the letters have been steered wrongly into a new order

explanation.surface: A carpenter wasted his time hunting for a good English chisel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' rearranges GOOD, E, CHISEL and WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild-goose chase is an idiom for a futile search after something unattainable.

clue.text: Concluding activity in the ring

definitions.meaning: settling or finalising, as in sealing a deal
boxers grappling to hold one another at close quarters

explanation.surface: The final round of a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinching a deal is settling it; in boxing a clinch is when fighters hold each other.

clue.text: Disregard an amnesty

definitions.meaning: neglect or forgetfulness, the state of being ignored
a general pardon, as in the Acts of ... after the English Civil War

explanation.surface: Forgetting wrongs through a general pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is a state of forgetting or ignoring; historically an Act of Oblivion pardoned past offences.

clue.text: Old-fashioned backward paper

parts.note: behind means lagging, backward in progress
The Times is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper that has fallen out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own newspaper, The Times, supplies the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind the times is an idiom for being out of date in one's ideas.

clue.text: Difficult position — could be lethal

definitions.meaning: a post where one faces pressure or tough questions
the electric chair, used for executions

explanation.surface: A dangerous situation that might kill.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang the hot seat is the electric chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot seat is a place of pressure and scrutiny, and literally an electric chair for executions.

clue.text: The removal of all traces of age? Certainly!

parts.note: an era is an age, a period of history
sure is an informal yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asks if age wipes everything out, and is assured it does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasure is wiping something out so that nothing is left, as with a rubber.

clue.text: An earl could be thus beaten

definitions.meaning: the stock phrase ... earl, from the belt given at an earl's investiture

explanation.surface: A nobleman might be given a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: A belted earl wears the sword belt of his rank at investiture.
explanation.definitionFit: Belted means thrashed with a strap; earls were invested with a belt, hence the phrase belted earl.

clue.text: What dragomen do in winter — pretentiously!

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Guides chatting showily in the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman is an interpreter or guide in Arabic- or Turkish-speaking countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman's job is translating speech between languages for travellers.

clue.text: Caesar, for instance, in principle right

parts.note: a rule is a principle, a guiding standard

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar being judged correct in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the definition is by example, so 'for instance' belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar is an example of a sovereign who governed an empire.

clue.text: County side in trouble

indicators.note: the side piece goes inside the trouble piece

parts.note: care means worry or trouble
L for left, one side

explanation.surface: A county team in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: CLARE is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: One arrangement which is perfect!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is an agreement or arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone delighted by a flawless plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, matching a standard of excellence exactly.

clue.text: Another name for some half forgotten type of fuel

indicators.note: half of the word some is dropped, leaving only its first two letters

parts.note: a briquet, also spelt briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: Someone half-remembers the name of a kind of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half forgotten' drops ME from SOME, leaving SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, a name used beside one's real one.

clue.text: Note from a star

definitions.meaning: the fifth degree of the ...-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message sent by a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, and the Latin name for the Sun.

clue.text: Wild game returns in African province

indicators.note: the reversed game goes inside the province

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: Wildlife and hunting come back to a South African region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RU into UR, placed 'in' NATAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means untamed, existing in nature without human influence.

clue.text: In idle wandering he follows, for example, a highbrow

indicators.note: the container piece follows the example piece
the word he goes inside the wandering piece

parts.note: to gad is to wander about idly, seeking pleasure

explanation.surface: An intellectual drifting aimlessly behind someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'idle wandering' is one idea, the verb gad; 'In' and 'follows' are the placement words, making GHEAD after the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is slang for an intellectual, someone bookish and cerebral.
